title: What Would Dragons Actually Change?
lesson: A monster changes a world through what ordinary people must do differently. A dragon hunts what it can see, so people hide from the sky (roofs that don't burn, covered barns, villages in valleys, travel by night), and once someone has to watch the sky, whoever watches holds power.

voice.direction: The same lab host, a shade darker for a predator episode. 'Because this is what a dragon sees' drops low and close. The target list is a calm, cold inventory. 'They just lived in plain sight' is the sting. The four changes are crisp. 'Look back' is the turn; 'Whoever rings it runs the village' is a quiet reveal. The comment ask is genuinely curious.

lines.text: If dragons existed, your world's architecture would look very different.
Because this is what a dragon sees.
Every thatch roof, open pen and cart: a target.
Week one: roofs burn. Week two: flocks gone. Week three: nobody travels.
Nobody fought a war. They just lived in plain sight.
So hide the village. Four changes are easy. The fifth is the twist.
One: roofs. Slate and turf don't burn.
Two: pens. Flocks sleep in covered barns.
Three: place. Build in the valley, under the cliff.
Four: travel. Move at night, under the trees.
The dragon looks down, and finds nothing.
A watchtower sees the dragon first. One bell, and everyone hides.
Whoever rings it runs the village. The dragon changed who's in charge.
Don't just add a dragon. Ask what ordinary people do differently.
What would your civilization invent to survive dragons? Comment below.
Part 27 of 50. Follow for part 28: something on the Isle learns to build.

shots.purpose: Pay off EP26's loop and stop the scroll: the dragon is here, and we ride on its back. Then switch to its eye.
shots.visual: Over the dragon's shoulder as it glides a wide circle over the open village in golden light; the Grimmaw looks up from its meadow; a cairn stands below. On 'sees' the frame turns to the DRAGON'S-EYE VIEW (red vignette, scanlines). The field card names it: DRAGON · HUNTS anything it can see.
shots.camera: Follow camera: over its shoulder (az −28 from behind, el 20, dist 17, fov 34); the last 10 s ride the same orbit back to this exact frame.

layers.background: the village, the meadow, the Isle

shots.onScreenText: IF DRAGONS / EXISTED → YOUR WORLD / WOULD LOOK / DIFFERENT. → DRAGON'S-EYE VIEW
shots.music: Soar: horns in open fifths, a taiko wingbeat, the theme low on horns; a hit on 'different', a stab on 'sees'.

shots.purpose: Show the stakes in the dragon's own terms: everything in the open is a target.
shots.visual: Still riding: red brackets lock onto every thatch roof, both flocks in their open pens, the village itself and each cart on the road; TARGETS counts up to 16. The sim bar slides in and RUN is pressed.
shots.camera: Follow camera, then rise to the wide on 'run'.
shots.music: Mystery: celesta arpeggios over a held pad, lock-on beeps.

shots.purpose: The naive village runs and fails, in numbers.
shots.visual: The whole Isle; the dragon circles low and fast; roofs char one by one and smoke; FLOCK 60→9; carts leave the road; WEEK 0→3.
shots.music: Raid: taiko eighths, low horn stabs, driving bass; a burn crackle bed.

shots.purpose: The punchline: no battle; they lived in plain sight.
shots.visual: Close on the burnt, empty village in gloom; the dragon glides home to its lair. COLLAPSED · NO WAR; IN PLAIN SIGHT.
shots.onScreenText: COLLAPSED · NO WAR · WEEK 3; IN PLAIN SIGHT.
shots.music: Drop to near silence; a taiko boom on 'sight'.

shots.purpose: Re-hook: rewind, then the job is to hide. Four easy changes and one locked twist.
shots.visual: REWIND; the village restored; the SKY-PROOF checklist (HIDE FROM THE SKY) with a blinking locked row 5.
Close on the houses; thatch flips to slate and turf one by one; each roof's red bracket flashes green and drops away; TARGETS 16→9.
shots.onScreenText: 1 ROOFS · slate and turf, not thatch

shots.visual: A covered barn rises over the open pen; both FLOCK brackets go green, HIDDEN; TARGETS 9→7.

shots.purpose: Change 3: get out of the sky's sight lines.
shots.visual: Near top-down; a red ring marks the open site; every building unbuilds and rises in the valley under the cliff, the flock follows; the VILLAGE bracket goes green; TARGETS 7→6.
shots.onScreenText: 3 PLACE · the valley, under the cliff

shots.purpose: Change 4: travel at night, under the trees.
shots.visual: Night; the road moves into the forest; lanterns on; the last cart brackets go green; TARGETS 00 · HIDDEN FROM THE SKY.
shots.onScreenText: 4 TRAVEL · by night, under the trees

shots.purpose: The hidden village runs, and the dragon's own eye proves it.
shots.visual: Wide, then over the dragon's shoulder above the valley in DRAGON'S-EYE VIEW: no brackets, TARGETS 00, NOTHING TO HUNT; the flock grows to 92, trade to 9.
shots.music: Drive with the theme on flute and glockenspiel; a stab and cymbal on 'nothing'.

shots.purpose: The locked rule: look back. The village watches the sky.
shots.visual: RULE 5? / LOOK BACK.; a stone watchtower rises on the cliff; WATCHTOWER VIEW (blue): from behind its bell, a blue bracket locks on the dragon far out over the coast, DRAGON · SPOTTED; the bell swings and the carts vanish (everyone hides).
shots.camera: Medium on the cliff (dist 74), then the tower's view (az −62, el 6, fov 32).
shots.onScreenText: RULE 5? LOOK BACK.; WATCHTOWER VIEW; DRAGON · SPOTTED
shots.music: Twist (held A7♭9, timpani), then soar as the dragon comes in; the tower bell; a hard stop on 'hides'.

shots.visual: Row 5 unlocks (WATCH · the bell-ringer runs it); close on the tower and bell; NEW POWER / THE BELL-RINGER; trade comes back; ripple on 'charge'.
shots.music: Swell into a big D-major hit on 'charge'.

shots.purpose: The takeaway: the full checklist, screenshot-able.
shots.visual: The complete SKY-PROOF card (BEFORE YOU ADD A DRAGON) with 'Ask what ordinary people change.' in serif italic.
shots.transition: Block wipe to the end card.
shots.music: Anthem: the theme in D major; the World Engine chime as the card lands.

shots.visual: End card: logo, PART 27 / 50, title, a speech-bubble COMMENT panel.
shots.camera: Cut (under the block wipe) back onto the dragon's shoulder, on its hook orbit.
shots.music: Outro: the theme's answer on celesta and music box.

graphics.title: What Would Dragons Actually Change?
graphics.with: What would your civilization invent to survive dragons?

shots.purpose: Say the part number, ask for the follow with a reason (part 28), open the next loop.
shots.visual: Riding the dragon's circle again; PART 27/50; FOLLOW FOR PART 28 pressed on 'Follow'; NEXT RUN 28 · BUILDERS from a locked cairn; below, a cairn's three stones stack themselves; the orbit lands on frame 0 and the hook title returns.
shots.camera: The follow camera on the hook orbit, landing on frame 0.

layers.foreground: progress bar, follow button, next-run card

shots.onScreenText: PART 27/50 · FOLLOW FOR PART 28 · NEXT RUN: BUILDERS · SOMETHING LEARNS TO BUILD.
shots.music: Tease over a held A, a horn call, the engine chime on 'Follow'; it resolves into frame 0's D minor.

music.key: D minor, resolving to D major

If dragons existed, your world's architecture would look very different. Because this is what a dragon sees: every thatch roof, every open pen, every cart on the road is a target.

We ran it. Week one, the roofs burn. Week two, the flocks are gone. Week three, nobody travels. Nobody fought a war; they just lived in plain sight.

So hide the village: slate and turf roofs, flocks in covered barns, the village moved into the valley under the cliff, and travel at night under the trees. Run it again, and the dragon looks down and finds nothing.

Then the twist: look back. A watchtower sees the dragon first; one bell, and everyone hides. Whoever rings it runs the village. The dragon changed who's in charge.

Don't just add a dragon. Ask what ordinary people do differently.
